chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: DePriest Wheeler and the bass trombone
summary: Jackson never saw Wheeler's bass trombone, having only subbed in his place and joined after Wheeler left.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: How about Dupreez Wheeler? Did you know him? He played trombone and bass trombone. I think he was one of the first bass trombone players I ever saw. He had a bass trombone and -- for me -- in Cab's band.
Oh, yeah? I never saw it. I didn't even know DePriest Dupreez had one.
I never saw it. Because the first bass trombone player I ever saw in a jazz band was with Stan Kenton. That was the first one I saw.
Well, DePriest Dupreez had one, with that
Uh-huh. I didn't know he had that.

Well, you know, I worked in Dupreez's place once when I first came to New York. I worked in his place at the Lafayette Theater and doubled at the Cotton Club. I used to talk to him when I was seeing him but very seldom I seen him because Calloway's band was always on the road and always gone.
And when I come to take his place in the band, he was gone, too. He had left. Because I joined the band in Springfield, Massachusetts, and he had left.
